transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-14 15:00 PST | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Maya, Diego, Renee (Redwood) / Lena, Marcus, Priya, Tom, Ellen (Orchard)

00:00 Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda: handoff to implementers, confirm pilot, runbook, and security checklist. We'll leave time for networking questions.
00:18 Lena (CTO): Yep, thanks. We're trying to fast-track a pilot in EU region and want to be clear on what you need from our side. Latency is a big one for us, p95 under 120 ms is the goal.
00:32 Diego (SE): Got it. For p95 120 ms we generally recommend Dedicated in-region or Private if you want strict data residency and control. There's a bunch of levers — batching, KV cache, quantization — that affect observed latency/cost.
00:46 Marcus (Platform Eng): Can you explain batching vs KV cache again? I've seen both but unclear tradeoffs.
00:54 Diego (SE): Sure. Batching groups requests to improve throughput — good for throughput but increases tail latency if your traffic is spiky. KV cache is prefix caching of context, which can drastically reduce tokens generated for repeated prompts. For interactive low-latency apps we bias toward small batch sizes + prefix cache.
01:12 Priya (Security): On the security front, we need to validate encryption in transit at TLS 1.3, KMS/HSM integration, and retention policies. Also SSO: we use SAML with Okta. Does Redwood support SAML/RBAC?
01:27 Maya (AE): Yes, we support SAML/SSO and RBAC; we'll provide the SAML metadata and a sample config. For KMS, we have integrations and our Private offering supports customer-managed keys in KMS/HSM. We'll share the security pack.
01:40 Tom (SRE): Regarding network, if we do Private in our VPC, what's the egress pattern? Do you require inbound rules? How is the control plane managed?
01:53 Diego (SE): For Private we ship a customer-managed control plane option: agents run in your VPC, outbound to a control channel if you opt in; alternatively, fully air-gapped mode is possible with an on-prem bundle. We'll send a network diagram. You need to allow egress to certain Redwood endpoints for telemetry unless air-gapped.
02:08 Ellen (PM): Pilot scope question: how many models, expected routes, and dataset size?
02:15 Marcus (Platform Eng): Initial ask is 3 routes — chat, summarization, and embeddings re-rank. Peak QPS expected around 18, burst to 60. Token mix varies, avg seq len 420 tokens.
02:28 Diego (SE): Great — that profile maps well. For those numbers, Dedicated reserved capacity in eu-west plus caching should be cost-effective. If you require strict data residency and control of keys, Private is the choice.
02:41 Lena (CTO): Budget is moderate. We'd like to start Hosted to iterate quickly, then move to Private for production. Is that a common flow?
02:49 Maya (AE): Very common. Hosted for the early pilot, transition to Dedicated/Private for production. We'll show migration patterns and how model version pinning works in the Console.
03:05 Priya (Security): On compliance, can you provide SOC2 type II report, pen test summaries, and audit log retention options? Also, who has access to raw prompts on your side?
03:18 Renee (CSM): We'll share SOC2 and pen test artifacts. Access to raw prompts depends on deployment: Hosted transcripts are retained per your tenancy settings and we offer options to redact or disable logging; Private means logs stay in your environment if you choose. We'll include the data retention matrix.
03:35 Marcus (Platform Eng): For the model runtime, are there recommendations on quantization? We're running on mixed CPU/GPU infra in our lab.
03:44 Diego (SE): We recommend Q4_8bit for many LLMs to balance memory and perf; but we test per model. Our Optimize toolkit suggests quantization profiles per workload and we can run a quick benchmark for you.
03:58 Lena (CTO): Will you run latency benchmarks in our environment or do you need sample traffic?
04:05 Diego (SE): Best is to run a small shadow test: we can provide a benchmark harness you deploy in your VPC to hit a Dedicated or Private staging node. Send us a representative traffic trace and we'll mimic distribution.
04:18 Tom (SRE): Ok. What about failover? If a region is overloaded, can you route to another region automatically? That matters for user-facing SLAs.
04:27 Maya (AE): Yes, Smart routing can failover to a compatible model/region per policy. We can configure latency-based routing or cost-based fallbacks with alerts. We also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller models if capacity constrained.
04:43 Ellen (PM): What's the normal timeline to go from pilot to production if we pick Private?
04:50 Maya (AE): Pilot to production is commonly 6–10 weeks depending on network work and compliance gating. If you want Dedicated it's faster ~4–6 weeks. Air-gapped Private can add extra time for package installation and certs.
05:05 Marcus (Platform Eng): On the Console, can we see token-level cost and route-level latencies?
05:11 Renee (CSM): Yes, Console gives token breakdown, per-model latency histograms, and traces. We'll attach sample screenshots in the runbook.
05:22 Priya (Security): A practical ask: can you draft an example Data Processing Agreement snippet around ephemeral storage and logs? Our legal will want that.
05:31 Maya (AE): We'll include a DPA template and the recommended language for ephemeral storage and log retention.
05:40 Lena (CTO): Anything else blocking us from starting the pilot next week?
05:45 Marcus (Platform Eng): We need the runbook and the network checklist, and I'll confirm the traffic trace.
05:51 Maya (AE): Action items captured — we'll send runbook and network diagram. Diego will set up the tech deep dive and Renee will open the pilot credit.
06:00 Diego (SE): Quick note — when you provide traffic, include seq length distribution, tokenization logs if possible, and which prompts are hot keys for cache tuning.
06:12 Tom (SRE): Will do.
06:15 Ellen (PM): Any final questions?
06:18 Priya (Security): One: for KMS keys, do we rotate on our schedule and can we revoke access independently?
06:25 Diego (SE): Yes for Private you control keys and can rotate per your schedule; revocation is supported with immediate denial of access. For Hosted we support customer-managed keys in some plans — we'll clarify in the security pack.
06:38 Lena (CTO): Great, thanks. This was helpful.
06:43 Maya (AE): Recap: Maya share runbook and DPA; Diego schedule deep-dive and share network diagram; Marcus deliver traffic profile; Priya list compliance owners; Renee open pilot credit and pricing sheet. We'll reconvene after the tech deep-dive to finalize pilot start date.
06:58 Meeting end.
